answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the mirror schedule in the signal ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the ledge checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 194 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
